title: ר' יעקב בן בתו של אלישע אחר

paragraphs: R. Yaakov, the son of Elisha Aḥer's daughter. Yuḥasin [in Seder HaDorot] writes that he is a tanna in chapter 4 of Nega'im (I did not find him there). The book abbreviated שנ״ח, parashat Tetze (4b), cites the Gemara in Kiddushin (39b): Rava said, 'Whose view is this? It is R. Yaakov's, who says that there is no reward for a commandment in this world,' etc. This R. Yaakov is the son of Elisha Aḥer's daughter. In the aforementioned book (201a) it says, 'And perhaps R. Yaakov ben Elisha'; likewise there, on side b, and on that same side, 'But R. Yaakov ben Elisha holds ...'; and there, on side c, 'And one may further say that R. Yaakov ben Elisha holds ...' They are one person: this is R. Yaakov ben Elisha. It also writes thus in parashat Lekh Lekha, 10b and c: R. Yaakov ben Elisha three times. In parashat Vayera, 17c, it has R. Yaakov bar Idi. Heaven forbid that one should say this! Examine my work on Seder HaDorot: it is merely a scribal error. He upheld [reward in] the life of the world to come [the wording בכ״מ is uncertain]. At the end of Ḥullin (142a) and in the first chapter of Kiddushin (39b), the wording is: 'Had Aḥer interpreted this verse as did R. Yaakov, his daughter's son, he would not have sinned.' In the Jerusalem Talmud, chapter 2 of Ḥagigah, halakhah 1, and there in the aforementioned Kiddushin: 'Elisha Aḥer saw R. Ḥutzpit's tongue in a pig's mouth. He said: Is this Torah, and is this its reward? Apparently there is no granting of reward, for it is written, "And you shall prolong your days." He went astray. He did not know that R. Yaakov had interpreted it before him: "And you shall prolong your days"—in the future that is wholly long.' End of quotation. He expounded this because he saw that his maternal grandfather Elisha had erred in this matter. Perhaps the wording 'R. Yaakov before him' is a scribal error and should read 'his daughter's son.' In Responsa Halakhot Ketanot, part 2, §249, he transcribes that Jerusalem Talmud passage, 'before him,' etc., and writes there: 'Between R. Yaakov and R. Shimon, the law follows R. Shimon, since he is mentioned more often in the Mishnah and baraita. But in truth the law follows R. Yaakov, since he was older than R. Shimon: R. Shimon was R. Akiva's student, and R. Akiva lived in Aḥer's time; thus R. Yaakov was older than R. Shimon.' End of quotation. In my opinion, this does not prove that R. Yaakov was older than R. Shimon, for Elisha's daughter lived in Rabbi's days, while R. Shimon was Rabbi's teacher. In Ruth Rabbah, at the verse 'Stay the night,' and in Kohelet Rabbah, at 'Better is the end of a thing than its beginning,' it has 'He did not know that R. Akiva had expounded it'; so too Yalkut Kohelet, at that verse, has 'R. Akiva bar sih [בר סיה].' In my opinion this is a scribal error and should read 'R. Yaakov, his daughter's son.' It appears that he is the one who says in Avot, in the chapter beginning Ben Zoma, 'This world resembles an antechamber.' Yet I find it difficult to say this, because in that chapter of Ben Zoma, after this it says 'Elisha ben Avuyah says'; how could it put the words of his daughter's son, R. Yaakov, before those of Elisha ben Avuyah? Admittedly, it did not maintain chronological order in that chapter: it gives Ben Zoma, then Ben Azzai, then Levitas of Yavneh, then R. Yoḥanan ben Berokah, then R. Yishmael, then R. Tzadok, then R. Yose, then R. Yishmael son of R. Yose, then R. Yonatan, then R. Meir, then R. Eliezer ben Yaakov, then R. Yoḥanan the Sandalmaker, R. Elazar ben Shammua, R. Yehudah, R. Nehorai, R. Yannai, R. Matya ben Ḥarash, R. Yaakov, and R. Shimon ben Elazar. Shemuel HaKatan, who lived in the time of Rabban Gamliel the Elder, preceded them all in time, and afterward [in the chapter] comes Elisha ben Avuyah. Some say that he is the father of R. Eliezer ben Yaakov. This is not convincing, for we have not found this, nor does it say 'R. Eliezer bar [it should read: son of Rabbi] Yaakov said.' In my opinion there are demonstrative proofs and compelling arguments that one cannot say R. Eliezer ben Yaakov was the son of R. Yaakov, the son of Elisha's daughter. For R. Eliezer ben Yaakov was R. Akiva's student and R. Meir's teacher (see his entry), and it is known that Elisha Aḥer was R. Meir's teacher: how could the son of Elisha's daughter's son be R. Meir's teacher? Thus it is impossible to say that R. Eliezer ben Yaakov was the son of R. Yaakov, Aḥer's daughter's son. Understand this. Certainly, according to Yuḥasin and Be'er Sheva, who hold that R. Eliezer ben Yaakov was a colleague of Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai—and it is known that Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai attended Elisha Aḥer's circumcision—how could R. Eliezer ben Yaakov be the grandson of Elisha Aḥer's daughter? Rather, he is certainly someone else. It remains doubtful whether he is R. Yaakov of Kefar Ḥitya, who lived in R. Akiva's time, also [mentioned] in a baraita, a great and holy sage, R. Akiva's student and Rabbi's teacher (see his entry). In Ḥagigah (5b), he would regularly greet his teacher every day.
